requirement: Fetch every item from a paginated REST listing by following the next link in each response's Link header, with a cap on the number of pages and clear errors for malformed pages.
skeleton: A page budget constant, a PaginationError, and fetch_all looping over pages with raise_for_status, a list check, extending items, following resp.links next, dropping params after the first request, and raising when the budget runs out.
caption: Paging through a JSON list API with requests by following RFC 8288 Link headers. PaginationError is a RuntimeError subclass. fetch_all(session, url, *, params=None, max_pages=MAX_PAGES, 50, timeout=10.0) loops at most max_pages times: it calls session.get with the current URL, query params and timeout, calls raise_for_status so HTTP errors raise requests.HTTPError, and parses JSON. A page that is not a list raises PaginationError. Items are extended onto the result, then resp.links next url becomes the next URL; when there is none the items are returned. After the first request params are set to None because the next link already carries the query. Running out of pages raises PaginationError. The fixture asserts, against a local server that rejects repeated query parameters, that five items arrive over three pages, that exactly max_pages pages are allowed, that an endless listing raises PaginationError after 50 requests by default, that an object page raises PaginationError, and that a 500 raises requests.HTTPError.

plan.intent: Mirror a remote collection into a local cache
constraints: Params are sent only on the first request
At most max_pages requests are made, default 50

rationale.teaches: Follow the server's next link via resp.links instead of computing offsets, drop initial params once the link carries them, and bound the loop.
rationale.why: Re-sending params duplicates the query, an unbounded loop hangs on a cyclic link, and unchecked pages silently merge dict keys into results.

ops.docstring: Collect every page of a JSON list API by following Link headers.

ops.source:
class PaginationError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when a listing is malformed or never ends."""

def fetch_all(
    session: requests.Session,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    max_pages: int = MAX_PAGES,
    timeout: float = 10.0,
) -> list[Any]:
    """Follow ``rel="next"`` links from ``url`` and concatenate each page."""
    items: list[Any] = []
    next_url = url
    query = params
    for _ in range(max_pages):
        resp = session.get(next_url, params=query, timeout=timeout)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        page = resp.json()
        if not isinstance(page, list):
            raise PaginationError(f"expected a JSON list from {next_url}")
        items.extend(page)
        link = resp.links.get("next", {}).get("url")
        if link is None:
            return items
        next_url = link
        query = None
    raise PaginationError(f"listing did not end within {max_pages} pages")

candidates.why_wrong: The initial params are re-sent with every next link, duplicating query keys.
A listing of exactly max_pages pages is rejected as endless.
The default budget allows 100 pages instead of 50.
A JSON object page is merged as its keys instead of raising.
A 500 error body is parsed as a page instead of raising HTTPError.
